How to use this calculator

  1. Enter weight, estimated body fat.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How lean body mass is calculated

Fat mass = body weight × body-fat fraction; lean body mass = body weight − fat mass. Because the input percentage is itself an estimate, any error in that percentage carries directly into the lean-mass result. At 80 kg and an estimated 20% body fat, lean mass is 80×0.80 = 64 kg.

Lean mass=weight×(1−body-fat fraction).
A worked example

At 80 kg and an estimated 20% body fat, lean mass is 80×0.80 = 64 kg.

Assumptions & useful context

Lean mass includes water, bone, organs, and muscle; it is not skeletal muscle mass alone.

Health calculations are estimates for education. They cannot diagnose a condition or replace a clinician’s assessment. Individual needs vary, especially during pregnancy, illness and growth.

Frequently asked questions

Is lean mass the same as skeletal muscle?

No. Lean mass includes water, organs, bone, and other non-fat tissue.

How accurate is the output?

It depends directly on the accuracy of the body-fat percentage you enter.
